research_status_text: Post-earnings update (Q3 2026, reported 2026-11-04), with the Intermex termination (2026-11-10) and Intermex's Delaware suit (2026-11-24)
stance_text: Watch — unchanged, bias now positive; fair value $8.62 at end-2029 including dividends (11.4% a year from $6.24); Own at about $5.67, Avoid above about $8.62. Q3 beat ($0.42 adjusted EPS against $0.34), the 2026 guide rose $0.03 and the Intermex deal is gone, which frees the cash it would have needed; the Delaware suit and a dividend that free cash flow barely covers keep the bear at 35% and a 15% cut chance inside the base
lens_text: Value at December 31, 2029: FY2029 adjusted EPS (adjusted operating income less net interest, taxed at 12-13%, over diluted shares) times an exit P/E (bear 3.5x, base 5.0x, bull 6.0x), plus dividends paid from the Q4 2026 payment through Q4 2029, less any Intermex litigation payment per share; undiscounted; cross-checked against 5.0x 2029 EBITDA less end-2029 net debt

bear.basis: North America retail keeps shrinking and digital pricing tightens: revenue -3.5% / -2% / -1% in 2027-2029 (the Saudi partner exit, NA retail at -6% adjusted, LACA transactions -12%); Beyond savings are spent on agent commissions and pricing, adjusted operating margin 14.5% / 14% / 14% (2026 about 15.4%); net interest $150-170M as the $1.4B of 2029 maturities refinance higher; 13% tax; shares +1.5% a year from stock awards with no buybacks. The board halves the dividend to $0.1175 a quarter from Q2 2027, and Western Union loses or settles Intermex's suit for $300M in 2027 (a court-ordered close at $16, about $500M plus Intermex's revolver for a business worth less than that to Western Union, or damages of similar size). 2029 adjusted EPS $0.94 x 3.5x = $3.31 + $1.76 of dividends - $0.96 litigation = $4.11

base.basis: Retail stabilizes slowly and digital growth offsets it from 2028: revenue -2% / 0% / +1% (2027 carries the Saudi account-payout exit); the $200M Beyond run-rate by end-2027 mostly offsets mix, adjusted operating margin 16% / 16.5% / 16.5% (2025 19.5%, Q3 2026 18%, 2026 about 15.4%); net interest $145-155M; 12% tax; shares +1% a year; $50M of Intermex settlement and legal cost in 2027. Free cash flow after $170-175M of capex covers the $0.235 quarterly dividend 0.94x / 1.06x / 1.05x, so the base keeps a 15% chance that the board halves it from Q2 2027 anyway; base dividends are the weighted $2.86 ($3.05 held, $1.76 halved). 2029 adjusted EPS $1.36 x 5.0x = $6.81 + $2.86 of dividends - $0.16 = $9.51

bull.basis: Migration flows recover and partnerships (Canada Post, Deutsche Post, Verizon Total Wireless) add volume: revenue 0% / +2% / +3%; Beyond savings drop through, adjusted operating margin 17% / 18% / 18.5% (still below 2025's 19.5%); net interest $140M; buybacks of $100M a year resume in 2028-2029 once gross leverage is inside 3.0x; Intermex's suit fails. Dividend held. 2029 adjusted EPS $1.91 x 6.0x = $11.45 + $3.05 of dividends = $14.50

horizon_text: Value at December 31, 2029, undiscounted, plus dividends paid from the Q4 2026 payment through Q4 2029; 3.1 years after the 2026-11-23 price, annualized over the rule's 3 years

street.rating_text: Sell (18 analysts: 1 Buy, 11 Hold, 2 Sell, 4 Strong Sell)
street.source: StockAnalysis forecast page (S&P Global Market Intelligence), sources/stockanalysis-forecast-2026-11-24.html.gz

deviation_from_street.reason: Our $8.62 is an end-2029 value that includes about $2.51 a share of weighted dividends; the Street's $6.73 mean is a 12-month price target. On price alone our weighted end-2029 value is $6.51, 3% below the Street's mean, so we do not disagree with the Street on what the shares will trade at. The gap is the dividend: at a 15% yield the market prices a cut as close to certain, while we put a cut before the end of 2027 at about 40% (the bear's 35% plus 15% of the base), because the Intermex termination frees the roughly $500M of cash (plus Intermex's revolver repayment) the deal would have used and the Beyond savings lift 2028-2029 free cash flow back to about 1.05x the dividend.

thesis: Q3 was better than feared and the balance sheet got lighter, but the business is not growing. Adjusted EPS was $0.42 against a $0.34 consensus, the adjusted operating margin recovered to 18% from 13-15% in the first half, and the 2026 guide rose to $1.28-$1.38; part of the beat was expense timing, and Q4 loses a low-margin Saudi account-payout partner that supplied about half of Branded Digital's growth. On November 10 Western Union walked away from Intermex under the outside date, so it no longer needs about $500M of cash plus Intermex's debt repayment; on November 24 Intermex sued in Delaware for specific performance. The call values the shares at end-2029 on adjusted EPS times a low multiple plus dividends: $4.11 / $9.51 / $14.50 at 35/45/20 gives $8.62, 11.4% a year from $6.24, Watch with a positive bias. On price alone the value is $6.51, below October's $7.30: the business view did not improve, the dividend is what makes the return. The bear is a dividend cut plus a $300M litigation cost. Own at about $5.67.
consensus_view: Eighteen analysts (S&P Global, as of November 13) rate the stock Sell: 1 Buy, 11 Hold, 2 Sell, 4 Strong Sell, with a $6.73 mean target ($6.00-$8.50, median $6.50); Cantor ($6, Sell), Barclays ($6, Sell) and J.P. Morgan ($7, Sell) reiterated after the termination and UBS raised to $6.50 from $6.25 at Hold. Consensus adjusted EPS is $1.32 for FY2026 and $1.46 for FY2027 on revenue of $4.00B and $4.11B; the FY2027 figures were last updated three days after the termination and may still include Intermex. 19.3% of shares are sold short. The stock rose 6.5% to $7.02 the day after the Q3 report, fell to $5.92 on November 20 and closed at $6.24 on November 23; the 15% yield says the market expects a cut.
variant_view: We agree with the Street on price: our weighted end-2029 value without dividends is $6.51 against its $6.73 12-month mean. We disagree on the dividend. At $6.24 and a 15.1% yield the market treats the $0.94 as about to be cut; we put a cut before the end of 2027 at about 40%. The case for the dividend improved this month: dropping Intermex removes a cash outlay of roughly $500M plus Intermex's revolver, the $800M term loan was refinanced out to 2029, and the Beyond program is ahead of its $50M run-rate target, which in our base lifts free cash flow to about 1.05x the dividend in 2028-2029. It is not safe: the Street's $166.5M 2026 free-cash-flow estimate is far below the $293M dividend. Checkable (claim div-cut-2027, 0.40): if Western Union declares a quarterly dividend below $0.235 before December 31, 2027, the variant view is wrong.

notes: The October call was a backfill whose values were five-year prices before dividends ($7.30 weighted). This update states end-2029 values that include dividends, as the STLA and CNM calls do. On price alone the weighted end-2029 value is $6.51, below October's $7.30: the base's price is $6.81 against October's five-year $7.15 on nearly the same EPS ($1.36 against $1.30) at a lower multiple (5.0x against 5.5x). The rise to $8.62 is weighted dividends ($2.51) less weighted litigation ($0.41), not a better view of the business; the 'raise' action refers to the published value, not to the business.

FY2026 starts at revenue of about $3,990M (9M $3,005.2M plus a Q4 of about $985M, inside the -1% to -2% ex-Intermex guide on FY2025's $4,050.7M) and adjusted EPS of $1.33, the guide midpoint (Q4 implied $0.31-$0.41 against $0.45 in 4Q25). Adjusted EPS each year is (revenue x adjusted operating margin - net interest + $3M other income) x (1 - tax) / diluted shares from 313.5M (Q3 diluted weighted average). Adjusted figures exclude Beyond program costs, severance, acquisition costs and the non-cash tax charge from the international reorganization (about $45M a year), as the guide and the Street do.

Exit multiples are on adjusted EPS: 3.5x / 5.0x / 6.0x. capital.multiples gives WU's own ten-year GAAP P/E bands of 3.9x (p10), 5.6x (p25) and 7.1x (median). The trailing gap between adjusted and GAAP EPS is about 35% ($1.42 against $1.05), but $0.12 of it is the one-off Beyond charge and FY2025 carried IRS settlement items; the recurring gap (the reorganization tax charge, about $0.13-0.15, plus small acquisition and severance items) is about 15-20%. At 15% the base's 5.0x is 5.8x GAAP, at 20% it is 6.0x, between WU's p25 and median; the bull's 6.0x is 6.9-7.2x GAAP, at the median. The SIC 7389 peer median (26.0x) is growth payments names and is not used; captured remittance peers IMXI (own median 15.8x) and EEFT (25.6x) sit above WU because they grew. The current forward P/E is 4.7x on the 2026 guide and 4.6x on base 2029 EPS.

Dividends count the Q4 2026 payment (ex-date expected in mid-December, after the call date) and twelve quarters of 2027-2029. A cut halves the quarterly $0.235 from Q2 2027 (the Q1 2027 dividend is declared with the Q4 results in February): $1.76 against $3.05 held. The bear cuts with certainty; the base cuts with a 15% chance (a cut in an otherwise base-case world, because base FCF covers the dividend only 0.94x in 2027 and gross leverage is above target) and carries the weighted $2.86; the bull holds. Across cases the chance of a cut before 2028 is 0.35 + 0.45 x 0.15 = 0.42, recorded as claim div-cut-2027 at 0.40. Litigation is deducted per share on today's diluted count: $0 / $50M / $300M.

Free cash flow (net debt path and coverage only) = adjusted net income + $60M before one-off cash items - cash restructuring ($30M in 2027, $10M after) - capex ($170-180M). FY2025 OCF was $543.7M on $574.6M of adjusted net income after about $200M of IRS settlement payments (about +$170M before them); 2026 OCF of about $456M (9M $321.2M plus a Q4 of $135M, the median of 2022-2025 fourth quarters from SEC facts) is about $37M above 2026 adjusted net income of about $419M after about $30M of Beyond severance (+$67M before it). The Street's $166.5M 2026 FCF (StockAnalysis) implies OCF near $357M; if that is right, coverage is weaker than the base and the FY2026 cash flow in February is the test. Base coverage of the dividend is 0.94x / 1.06x / 1.05x in 2027-2029 and end-2029 net debt is $1,833M (2.2x EBITDA).

Sensitivities (printed by the build script): weights 30/50/20 $8.89 (12.5%), 40/45/15 $8.10 (9.1%), 45/40/15 $7.83 (7.9%), 25/50/25 $9.41 (14.7%); base exit P/E 4.0x $8.00, 4.5x $8.31, 5.5x $8.92, 6.0x $9.23; base dividend halved from Q2 2027 with certainty $8.12 (9.2%), suspended $7.54 (6.5%), held with certainty $8.70 (11.7%); base 2028-29 margin 15% $8.25, 17.5% $8.86; base litigation $0 $8.69; bear litigation $600M $8.28 (9.9%). Cross-check at 5.0x 2029 EBITDA less net debt plus dividends less litigation: $5.59 / $10.05 / $13.66.

The $200M end-2027 Beyond run-rate target dates from the program's July 2026 launch and is recorded in the October initiation (research/WU.md); the Q3 call said the company is ahead of the $50M year-end target and 'setting us up well to deliver against our 2027 Beyond Efficiency targets' (sources/news-excerpts-2026-11-24.txt).
The November 24 close of $6.22 (StockAnalysis) was not yet in data/prices/WU.csv when the call was written; the call uses the November 23 close of $6.24.
Peers captured for this update: IMXI, EEFT and RELY monthly prices and SEC facts (capital.multiples capture and capital.sec).

Review round 1 (agent:reviewing-research, grade B): the first draft ($4.31 / $9.70 / $14.50, fair value $8.77, 12.0% a year) gave the base an intact dividend with certainty while its own FCF covered it 0.94x in 2027, set the bear's cut from Q1 2027 against a 0.80 claim that Q1 holds, sized the bear's Intermex cost at $200M against a 20% chance of a forced close, did not reconcile its 2026 OCF with the Street's $166.5M FCF, and assumed a 15% adjusted-to-GAAP gap without addressing the 35% trailing gap. All addressed as described in review.response.

low_score_reasons: evidence: The base's dividend coverage depends on 2026 operating cash flow of about $470M, which assumes a Q4 like 2025's $135M, but the saved StockAnalysis page shows a 2026 free-cash-flow consensus of $166.5M, implying operating cash flow near $357M after $190M of capex; the projection lists that figure, yet the call and update note never reconcile it, and the $200M Beyond end-2027 target traces only to the initiation, not to this run's sources.

valuation: The bear weight is set equal to the 0.35 dividend-cut claim, which assumes a cut only ever comes with 14% margins, a 3.5x multiple and a $200M payment and never in the base, even though the base's own free cash flow covers the dividend just 0.94x in 2027 while gross leverage stays above the 2.5-3.0x target; the bear also starts the cut in Q1 2027, while div-235-q1-27 at 0.80 puts no more than 20% on a cut by then, and the exit-multiple defense assumes adjusted EPS runs 15% above GAAP when the trailing gap is about 35% ($1.42 against $1.05), which puts 5.0x adjusted nearer WU's 7.1x GAAP median than its 5.6x 25th percentile.

risk: The call's own claim (imxi-no-close-2027 at 0.80) gives a 20% chance that Western Union completes Intermex or is ordered to, and a kill criterion fires on that outcome, yet no scenario models a close or a payment above $200M (the $500M case is only a sensitivity), so the litigation is undersized against the call's own probabilities, especially given Intermex's allegation that the DFPI conditionally approved the deal the same evening Western Union terminated.
review.counter_case: On a like-for-like basis the business view fell: the price-only value is $6.51, against October's $7.30, so the 'raise' and the positive bias come entirely from counting $3.05 of undiscounted dividends that a 15% yield says the market doubts. The dividend is weaker than a 35% cut probability implies: the saved Street estimate puts 2026 free cash flow at $166.5M against a dividend of about $293M, the call's own base covers it only 0.94x in 2027, and gross leverage is 3.3x against a 2.5-3.0x target with $1.4B maturing in 2029, from a board that has already paused buybacks to protect leverage. A cut in an otherwise base-case world takes the base to $6.88 and fair value to $7.51 (the suspended-dividend sensitivity), only 6.3% a year with the bear and bull unchanged. A Delaware loss or a forced close at $16, which the call itself puts at 20%, would add debt at exactly that moment.
review.response: Accepted on the dividend, litigation and evidence points; fair value cut from $8.77 (12.0% a year) to $8.62 (11.4%). The base now carries a 15% chance that the dividend is halved from Q2 2027 in an otherwise base-case world, so base dividends are the weighted $2.86 and the base is $9.51; the overall chance of a cut before 2028 is 0.42 and claim div-cut-2027 moves to 0.40. The bear's cut starts in Q2 2027, after the Q1 declaration, and div-235-q1-27 moves to 0.85. The bear's Intermex cost rises to $300M to stand for a forced close or damages of similar size; the $600M case is a sensitivity ($8.28). The 2026 OCF is now the median of 2022-2025 Q4s ($135M) for about $456M, and the notes and update note set it against the Street's $166.5M FCF (OCF near $357M), naming FY2026 cash flow in February as the test. The $200M Beyond target is sourced to the initiation and the Q3 call. On the multiple: the 35% trailing adjusted-to-GAAP gap includes the one-off $0.12 Beyond charge; the recurring gap is 15-20%, putting the base's 5.0x at 5.8-6.0x GAAP, between WU's p25 and median, and the notes say so. On the counter-case: we agree the business view fell (price-only $6.51 against $7.30) and the notes and update note now say the raise is the dividends, net of litigation. We keep Watch with a positive bias because even with the base dividend suspended the weighted value returns 6.5% a year, and at 45/40/15 7.9%; the stance only reaches Avoid if the bear's weight rises well past half.
